name: sonnet-v2-3
how: Each session: a fresh Claude Code subagent that could read only the rendered prompts (one file per case), answered them in order and wrote its answers to a file. No API key; nothing else in its context.

answers.test: cancel returns to the cart @regression
answers.reason: The test clicks Cancel but asserts nothing afterwards, so Cancel going anywhere would still pass.

answers.test: cancel returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: It clicks Cancel on the overview and asserts the URL is inventory.html.

answers.test: inventory is blocked after logout @regression
answers.reason: After logout it visits /inventory.html and asserts the error contains the exact required text.

answers.test: cart badge is cleared after finishing @regression
answers.reason: After finishing, it asserts the cart badge count is 0.

answers.test: removing a product decrements the badge @regression
answers.reason: It adds two items, removes one and asserts the badge is 1.

answers.test: user stays logged in on the products page after reset @regression
answers.reason: It asserts the URL is inventory.html and the title is Products after reset.

answers.test: clicking a product name opens its details page @smoke
answers.reason: It clicks a product name link and asserts the URL is that item's details page.

answers.test: details page shows the same name and price as the list @regression
answers.reason: It compares name and price only for the first product, so a wrong item or data for other products would not be caught.

answers.test: inventory is blocked after logout @regression
answers.reason: It only checks that some error is visible, not that it contains the required message, so a wrong message would pass.

answers.test: total is $32.39 @regression
answers.reason: It only checks the label contains 'Total: $', so a wrong total amount would pass.

answers.test: item stays in the cart after opening another product @smoke
answers.reason: It opens another product's details, then checks the cart still lists the Backpack.

answers.test: valid credentials redirect to the products page @smoke
answers.reason: It logs in with valid credentials and asserts the URL is inventory.html.

answers.test: login button is visible again after logout @regression
answers.reason: The URL test is vacuous, but the login-button visibility test would fail if logout did not return to the login page.

answers.test: cart badge is cleared after finishing @regression
answers.reason: The only test for the badge is skipped, so nothing checks it.

answers.test: missing last name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: It fills only the first name, continues and asserts the exact Last Name required error.

answers.test: six products are shown after sorting @regression
answers.reason: It sorts and asserts exactly 6 inventory items are shown.

answers.test: submitting an empty form shows username required @regression
answers.reason: It submits an empty form and asserts the error contains 'Username is required'.

answers.test: total is $32.39 @regression
answers.reason: It asserts the total label has exactly 'Total: $32.39'.

answers.test: six products are shown after sorting @regression
answers.reason: The count assertion is >= 0, which always passes, so no product count is checked.

answers.test: price low to high shows the Onesie first at $7.99 @regression
answers.reason: It sorts low to high and asserts the first item is the Onesie priced $7.99.

answers.test: missing first name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: It continues with empty fields and asserts the exact First Name required error.

answers.test: price low to high shows the Onesie first at $7.99 @regression
answers.reason: It checks the first item name but no longer checks the $7.99 price.

answers.test: tax is $2.40 @regression
answers.reason: It asserts the tax label reads exactly 'Tax: $2.40'.

answers.test: submitting an empty form shows username required @regression
answers.reason: It asserts the visible text 'Epic sadface: Username is required', which contains the required message.

answers.test: cart page is empty after reset @regression
answers.reason: After reset it opens the cart and asserts zero inventory items.

answers.test: finishing shows the Checkout: Complete! page @smoke
answers.reason: It asserts the complete URL and the visible 'Checkout: Complete!' text after Finish.

answers.test: adding a product sets the cart badge to 1 @smoke
answers.reason: The first test only checks the badge is visible, not that it shows 1; the two-product and remove tests only partly pin down the count.

answers.test: overview lists the backpack @smoke
answers.reason: It asserts the overview lists exactly the Sauce Labs Backpack.

answers.test: adding a product sets the cart badge to 1 @smoke
answers.reason: It asserts the badge reads 1 after adding, and the two-product test confirms incrementing.

answers.test: locked-out user sees a locked-out message @regression
answers.reason: It logs in as the locked-out user and asserts the error contains the required text.

answers.test: logout returns to the login page @smoke
answers.reason: After logout it asserts the URL is exactly the base login URL.

answers.test: removing the last item hides the badge @regression
answers.reason: It adds then removes the only item and asserts the badge count is 0.

answers.test: all fields filled continues to the overview @regression
answers.reason: It fills all fields, continues and asserts the title is Checkout: Overview.

answers.test: badge still counts the item after reloading @regression
answers.reason: It reloads the products page and asserts the badge still reads 1.

answers.test: item total is $29.99 @regression
answers.reason: It asserts the subtotal label reads exactly 'Item total: $29.99'.

answers.test: missing postal code shows an error @regression
answers.reason: It fills first and last name only and asserts the exact Postal Code required error.

answers.test: cancel returns to the cart @regression
answers.reason: It clicks Cancel and asserts the URL is cart.html.

answers.test: adding two different products shows a badge of 2 @regression
answers.reason: It adds two products and asserts the badge reads 2.

answers.test: finishing shows the Checkout: Complete! page @smoke
answers.reason: It clicks Finish and asserts the title is Checkout: Complete!.

answers.test: cart page lists the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: It adds two items, opens the cart and asserts both names in order.

answers.test: name Z to A shows the red T-shirt first @regression
answers.reason: It sorts Z to A and asserts the first item is the red T-shirt.

answers.test: back home returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: It clicks Back Home and asserts the URL is inventory.html.

answers.test: login button is visible again after logout @regression
answers.reason: It asserts the login button is visible after logout.

answers.test: default sort is name A to Z with Sauce Labs Backpack first @smoke
answers.reason: It asserts the sort value is az and the first item is the Backpack.

answers.test: details page shows the same name and price as the list @regression
answers.reason: The test never asserts anything about the details page, only that list values exist.

answers.test: checkout opens the Your Information step @smoke
answers.reason: It goes from cart to Checkout and asserts the title is Checkout: Your Information.

answers.test: incorrect password shows a credential mismatch error @regression
answers.reason: The test performs the login but has no assertion on the error.

answers.test: removing the last item hides the badge @regression
answers.reason: It only asserts the Products title, never that the badge is hidden.

answers.test: incorrect password shows a credential mismatch error @regression
answers.reason: It asserts the error contains 'Username and password do not match'.

answers.test: back to products returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: It clicks Back to products and asserts the URL is inventory.html.

answers.test: user stays logged in on the products page after reset @regression
answers.reason: It only checks the menu button is visible, which shows a logged-in state but not that the products page is shown.

answers.test: cart page matches the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: It only checks the cart has 2 items, not which items, so a wrong item would pass.

answers.test: products page displays at least one product after login @regression
answers.reason: It logs in and asserts the first inventory item is visible.

answers.test: adding from the details page sets the cart badge to 1 @regression
answers.reason: It adds from the details page and asserts the badge reads 1.

answers.test: price high to low shows the Fleece Jacket first at $49.99 @regression
answers.reason: It sorts high to low and asserts the first item is the Fleece Jacket at $49.99.

answers.test: missing last name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: It only checks the error contains 'required', so a wrong field's required message would pass.

answers.test: cart page matches the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: It asserts the cart lists exactly the Backpack and the Fleece Jacket.

answers.test: reset removes the cart badge @smoke
answers.reason: After reset with two items it asserts the badge count is 0.

answers.test: thank-you heading is shown @regression
answers.reason: It asserts the complete header reads exactly 'Thank you for your order!'.

answers.test: tax is $2.40 @regression
answers.reason: The loose /2.4/ regex matches wrong values such as $12.40 or $2.45, so only some wrong taxes would fail.

answers.test: login button is visible again after logout @regression
answers.reason: The assertion is wrapped in try/catch that swallows failure, so the test can never fail.

answers.test: adding two different products shows a badge of 2 @regression
answers.reason: The expect is not awaited, so the test can finish before the check runs and a wrong count would not fail it.

answers.test: cart page is empty after reset @regression
answers.reason: It counts 'cart-item' elements, which don't exist on the cart page, so the check always passes.

answers.test: adding from the details page sets the cart badge to 1 @regression
answers.reason: A wrong badge value fails, but a missing badge is skipped by the if-visible guard and passes.

answers.test: missing first name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: It only asserts the error is not the Last Name message, so no error or a wrong message still passes.

answers.test: badge still counts the item after reloading @regression
answers.reason: It reloads the products page via navigation and asserts the badge still reads 1.

answers.test: price high to low shows the Fleece Jacket first at $49.99 @regression
answers.reason: The test actually sorts low to high and checks the last item, so high-to-low sorting is never verified.
